'''Fraser Andrew Armstrong''' {{post-nominals|FRS}} is a professor of [[chemistry]] at the [[University of Oxford]]<ref name=scopus>{{Scopus id}}</ref> and a [[Fellow]] of [[St John's College, Oxford]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://research.chem.ox.ac.uk/fraser-armstrong.aspx|title=Professor F.A. Armstrong F.R.S.|work=ox.ac.uk|access-date=29 October 2011|archive-date=26 February 2019|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190226093456/http://research.chem.ox.ac.uk/fraser-armstrong.aspx|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.cambia.org/daisy/eos/4049.html|title=Fraser Armstrong|work=cambia.org|access-date=29 October 2011|archive-date=4 March 2016|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160304094522/http://www.cambia.org/daisy/eos/4049.html|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=The Armstrong Research Group |url=http://armstrong.chem.ox.ac.uk/ |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110417082349/http://armstrong.chem.ox.ac.uk/ |archive-date=2011-04-17 |access-date=2026-03-20 |website=armstrong.chem.ox.ac.uk}}</ref><ref name=oil>{{Cite book|title=Energy... beyond oil|date=2007|publisher=[[Oxford University Press]]|first1=Fraser|last1=Armstrong|first2=Katherine |last2=Blundell|author-link2=Katherine Blundell|isbn=9780199209965|location=Oxford|oclc=314220853}}</ref>

== Early life and education ==
Fraser Armstrong was born in Cambridge, England, in 1951. He obtained his [[Bachelor of Science]] degree in 1975 followed by a [[PhD]] in 1978 from the [[University of Leeds]]<ref name=whoswho>{{Who's Who | author=Anon| title=Armstrong, Prof. Fraser Andrew | id = U250518 | year = 2017 | doi =10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.250518 | edition = online [[Oxford University Press]]|location=Oxford}}</ref><ref name="DOI10.1021/ar00155a004">Fraser A. Armstrong, H. Allen O. Hill, Nicholas J. Walton: ''Direct electrochemistry of redox proteins.'' In: ''Accounts of Chemical Research.'' 21, 1988, p&nbsp;407–413, {{doi|10.1021/ar00155a004}}.</ref> supervised by Geoff Sykes.<ref>{{cite journal|journal=Polyhedron|title=A Tribute to Alfred Geoffrey (Geoff) Sykes FRS (1934–2007)|volume=27|year=2008|pages=1139–1140|doi=10.1016/j.poly.2007.12.009|last1=Richens|first1=David T.|issue=4|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Career and research ==
After his PhD, Armstrong carried out [[postdoctoral research]] with Peter Kroneck (Konstanz), Ralph Wilkins (New Mexico), [[Helmut Beinert]] (Madison), and [[Allen Hill (scientist)|Allen Hill]] (Oxford).{{citation needed|date=February 2018}}

In 1983 he was awarded a [[Royal Society University Research Fellowship]] which he held in Oxford until 1989, when he joined the Chemistry Faculty at the [[University of California, Irvine]]. He moved to his present position in 1993. His interests are in biological redox chemistry, in particular the application of dynamic electrochemical techniques in studies of complex electron-transfer and catalytic reactions in proteins ([[protein film voltammetry]]), and most recently the mechanisms and exploitation of biological hydrogen cycling. He was the president of the [[Society of Biological Inorganic Chemistry]] (SBIC) from 2004 to 2006. With [[Katherine Blundell]] he co-edited the book ''Energy... beyond Oil''.<ref name=oil/>
